title: Latin America's energy storage market to grow 13-fold by 2035, from 2.5 GW to 34 GW
gist: Wood Mackenzie forecasts Latin America's battery storage capacity will grow 13-fold from 2.5 GW (2025) to 34 GW (2035), a 30% CAGR driven by tender activity, renewable curtailment and weak transmission infrastructure, but warns that most markets still lack the bankable remuneration frameworks needed to convert announced pipeline into delivered capacity.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's Latin America energy storage outlook 2026 projects cumulative battery storage capacity in the region will grow from 2.5 GW in 2025 to 34 GW by 2035, a 13-fold increase representing a 30% compound annual growth rate.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 30% CAGR over a decade signals a large, investable buildout opportunity for battery storage developers, equipment suppliers and financiers targeting Latin America.
insights.quote: Wood Mackenzie’s Latin America energy storage outlook 2026 projects cumulative capacity will grow from 2.5 gigawatts (GW) in 2025 to 34 GW by 2035, a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 30%.

insights.claim: The primary drivers of Latin America's energy storage growth are accelerating tender activity, rising renewable curtailment, and unmodernized transmission infrastructure that cannot absorb growing renewable generation without storage support.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Storage economics in the region are being pulled by grid bottlenecks and curtailment losses rather than pure cost declines, meaning transmission and market-design fixes (or their absence) will directly gate deployment pace.
insights.quote: Accelerating tender activity, rising renewable curtailment and unmodernized transmission infrastructure are the primary forces behind this growth.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's Pamela Morales argues Latin America has shifted from a frontier to an active energy storage market, but cautions that deployment stalls without comprehensive regulatory frameworks that include clear remuneration mechanisms.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The bull case on regional storage capacity is conditional on regulatory follow-through, not just technology or tender momentum; investors should track remuneration-mechanism legislation as the key catalyst/risk.
insights.quote: Latin America is no longer a frontier market for energy storage, it is an active one. The pipeline is growing fast, but deployment stalls without comprehensive regulatory frameworks with clear remuneration mechanisms

themes.theme: Chile: leader with emerging cannibalisation risk

insights.claim: Chile remains Latin America's regional storage leader and hosts the largest operational battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in the region, with high renewable curtailment continuing to drive investment into longer-duration storage systems.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Chile is the most mature and largest near-term BESS market in the region, making it the primary near-term entry point for storage developers and equipment suppliers.
insights.quote: Chile remains the regional leader and holds the largest operational BESS projects in Latin America. High curtailment continues to drive investment in longer-duration systems.

insights.claim: In Chile's northern grid, price cannibalisation is emerging as a risk as more storage capacity enters the market, eroding the arbitrage revenues that have underpinned battery project economics.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: As Chile's storage pipeline matures, later-stage projects face compressing arbitrage margins, a revenue risk investors should model into IRR assumptions for new Chilean BESS assets, especially in the north.
insights.quote: However, price cannibalisation in the northern grid is an emerging risk, eroding arbitrage revenues as more storage enters the market.

insights.claim: Mexico's storage market is at a policy-driven inflection point, with new mandatory-storage mechanisms -- including the first priority call for proposals and a joint development call with the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) -- expected to award more than 3 GW of storage capacity by 2030.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Mexico is set to become a material near-term storage award market via state-linked tenders; investors and suppliers should track CFE tender timelines as a concrete 3+ GW opportunity through 2030.
insights.quote: Recent enabling mechanisms — including the first priority call for proposals and the joint development call with Mexico’s Federal Electricity Commission (CFE), both with mandatory storage — are expected to award more than 3 GW of storage capacity by 2030.

themes.theme: Brazil: tender ahead but bankability lag

insights.claim: Brazil is set for a significant storage market step forward via a dedicated battery tender scheduled for December 2026, which will drive capacity additions starting in 2028, though project financing will remain challenging near-term absent clear remuneration mechanisms.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Brazil's storage capacity ramp is real but delayed to 2028+ and financing-constrained until remuneration rules are clarified -- a catalyst to watch is the December 2026 tender outcome and any follow-on regulatory action on ancillary-service payments.
insights.quote: A dedicated battery tender, scheduled for December 2026, will drive capacity additions from 2028 onwards. However, without clear remuneration mechanisms, project financing will remain challenging in the near term.

themes.theme: Argentina and the Caribbean: standalone storage build-out

insights.claim: Argentina has moved quickly to build a standalone storage market through tenders, with recent rounds awarding a combined 1.3 GW of standalone storage capacity; operations are set to begin in 2027 to provide critical transmission support.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Argentina's 1.3 GW awarded pipeline with 2027 operational start gives investors a concrete near-term capacity ramp to track outside the larger Chile/Mexico/Brazil markets.
insights.quote: Recent rounds awarded a combined 1.3 GW of standalone storage. Operations are set to begin in 2027, providing critical transmission support.

insights.claim: The Dominican Republic has the most structured storage regulatory framework in the Caribbean, anchored by a 50% storage-to-solar capacity mandate, with the government targeting 500 MW of storage by 2030.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A binding storage-to-solar mandate makes the Dominican Republic a comparatively low-regulatory-risk Caribbean entry point for storage-plus-solar developers targeting the 500 MW 2030 target.
insights.quote: The Dominican Republic offers the most structured regulatory framework in the Caribbean. A 50% storage-to-solar capacity mandate drives near-term deployment, with the government targeting 500 megawatts (MW) by 2030.

themes.theme: Structural bankability risk across the region

insights.claim: Deployment across Latin America remains constrained by the absence of bankable revenue mechanisms and clear regulatory frameworks, with most markets lacking defined remuneration for ancillary services and energy arbitrage, compounded by restricted financing, permitting delays and limited offtakers.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The region-wide bottleneck is bankability, not technology or demand -- investors should prioritize markets with defined ancillary-service and arbitrage remuneration rules over those merely announcing pipeline.
insights.quote: Most markets lack defined remuneration for ancillary services and energy arbitrage, making long-term bankability difficult. Restricted financing, permitting delays and limited offtakers compound the challenge.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's Pamela Morales predicts the next decade will separate Latin American storage markets that merely announce capacity from those that build bankable revenue frameworks and successfully deliver it, arguing a balance between mandates and incentives is needed to sustain growth.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: This is a screening framework for investors: favor jurisdictions pairing mandates with incentive-based bankable revenue mechanisms, and treat headline GW pipeline figures with skepticism until remuneration rules are codified.
insights.quote: Latin America still needs to find a balance between mandates and incentives to develop the market. Countries that build bankable revenue frameworks will attract the investment needed to sustain growth well beyond the current policy-driven wave... The next decade will separate markets that merely announce capacity from those that successfully deliver it.
